composition: Nominal composition Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr (wt.%). Measured composition of the 3Cr strip (Table 1): 20.04 Mn, 9.09 Al, 1.23 C, 3.09 Cr, 0.0009 S, balance Fe (all in wt.%). The alloy is part of a controlled series in which Mn (20.04–20.43), Al (9.09–9.16) and C (1.17–1.23) are held nearly constant and Cr is deliberately stepped from 0 to 3.09 to 6.08 wt.%, so Cr is the single compositional variable. Fe-Mn-Al-C of this class is an austenite-based duplex (ferrite-containing) low-density steel in which Al lowers the density while Mn and C stabilize austenite and enable nano-scale κ-carbide precipitation; Cr was added to examine its influence on phase constitution and deformation behaviour. Starting charge purity: 99.99% Fe, 99.9% Mn, 99.9% Al, 99.9% Cr, 99.8% high-purity graphite; compositions were verified by ICP and a CS2800 carbon–sulfur analyzer.
summary: The as-cast 3Cr strip is the 3 wt.% Cr member of a controlled Cr-addition series of near-rapidly solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr (x = 0, 3, 6 wt.%) austenite-based duplex (TRIPLEX) steel strips, produced by centrifugal casting into a rotating copper mold. Relative to the Cr-free strip, the 3 wt.% Cr addition raises the δ-ferrite volume fraction to 12% (block morphology instead of short rods), promotes the δ-ferrite → ordered DO3 transformation, and markedly reduces the nano-scale κ-carbide population in the austenite; the resulting as-cast 3Cr strip has a significantly lower yield strength (642 MPa) at essentially unchanged total elongation (38%).
